title: GitHub Trending Weekly #28: NOMAD, Expect, OpenSpace, hyperspaceai, feynman, gea, lil-agents, optio

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This is GitHub Trending Weekly, episode 28. In this video, I've handpicked 33 trending open-source projects on GitHub. Let's get into it.

sections.title: Project NOMAD
paragraphs: Project Nomad stands for Node for Offline Media, Archives, and Data. And it's exactly what that sounds like. It's a self-contained Docker orchestrated web server designed to run completely without internet access. Through a single command center UI, you can pre-download full Wikipedia archives, detailed offline maps, survival and medical PDFs, and spin up a local AI assistant powered by OALMA.

sections.title: Expect
paragraphs: AI agents write front-end code without any way to verify it actually works in a browser. Expect closes that loop. It's a CLI skill for clawed code that automatically scans unstaged git changes or branch diffs, generates a test plan, and executes it against a real live browser. When your agent finishes building a feature, it tests the UI itself before opening a pull request. Your agent writes the code, checks that it works, then asks for review.

sections.title: OpenSpace
paragraphs: Every Claw Code session starts from scratch. Same mistakes, same token burn, no memory of what worked last time. OpenSpace runs alongside your agent and watches it work. When it successfully solves something complex, a weird TypeScript error, or a resilient data service, OpenSpace extracts that logic and saves it as a reusable skill in a local SQLite database. Next time a similar problem comes up, it feeds the solution back instantly.

sections.title: hyperspaceai
paragraphs: Hyperspace AI dropped the world's first peer-to-peer distributed AGI system. It is a living project constantly updated by thousands of autonomous AI agents. Just connect your browser or terminal to share your idle compute. Your machine collaboratively trains models and instantly shares breakthroughs globally. It's literally a decentralized AI hive mind.

sections.title: feynman
paragraphs: Fineman is a fully open-source AI research agent that runs entirely in your terminal built specifically for academic and ML research workflows. Instead of a single LLM answering questions, it runs a multi- aent system with dedicated researcher, reviewer, writer, and verifier roles working together. Give it a topic and it handles literature retrieval, peer review, code audits, and experimental replication autonomously.

sections.title: gea
paragraphs: Another JavaScript framework, yes, but the benchmarks on this one are hard to ignore. GIA ditches the virtual DOM entirely. Instead of a heavy runtime, it uses compile time.js JSX transforms and proxybased stores for what it calls surgical DOM patching. The key difference from other compiled frameworks like spelt when you change one item in a list GI mutates the proxied array in place and feeds that exact operation straight into a pre-ompiled DOM patcher.

sections.title: HyperAgents
paragraphs: Most self-improving AI systems have a hard-coded meta agent that rewrites task logic. Hyper agents from Metafare goes a level deeper. It unifies the tasks agent and the meta optimizing agent into a single self-referential program embedded in an evolutionary search loop. The system doesn't just rewrite what it does. It rewrites how it self-improves. The optimization mechanism itself is on the table.

sections.title: motrix-next
paragraphs: Motric is a beloved download manager that never got the maintenance it deserved. Motrix next fixes that same beautiful interface, same area 2 multi-threaded download engine underneath, but rebuilt from scratch on Tori 2 and Vue3. The Electron and Vue 2 stack is gone, and so is the memory overhead that came with it.

sections.title: lil-agents
paragraphs: Lil Agents puts two pixel art companions named Bruce and Jazz on your Mac OS doc. They walk back and forth across your apps, stop to think, and generally exist on your screen while you work. Click one and a Claude AI terminal slides open right on your desktop. Everything runs locally. No file paths or personal data sent anywhere. And the app dynamically calculates your doc size to position the characters correctly.

sections.title: flipoff
paragraphs: Want a $3,500 retro airport display for free? Someone tried charging 200 bucks for a web version, so a developer got mad and built FlipOff out of pure open- source spite. It runs entirely in your browser with zero dependencies. Just hit full screen to turn any monitor into a stunning mechanical flipboard complete with authentic clacking sounds.

sections.title: follow-builders
paragraphs: Follow builders is a clawed code skill that turns your agent into a personal intelligence analyst for the developers you actually want to track. Give it a list of builders you follow. It autonomously scans GitHub for their latest stars, commits, and new projects, and crawls the web for recent blog posts. Then it compiles everything into a personalized HTML daily digest that reads like a curated newspaper rather than a raw data dump.

sections.title: optio
paragraphs: Most AI coding tools write the code and stop. Optio keeps going until the PR merges. link it to a GitHub issue or linear ticket and it spins up an isolated Kubernetes pod, runs clawed code or codeex and opens a pull request. When the CI pipeline breaks, it feeds the error logs back to the agent to fix. When a human reviewer requests changes, it reads the comments and pushes a new commit.

sections.title: markit
paragraphs: Getting real world data into a format an LLM can actually read is one of those problems every agentic workflow eventually hits. Market is a universal convert anything to markdown CLI. Type market followed by a PDF, Word, Doc, PowerPoint, Excel file, EPUB, or live URL, and it pipes clean markdown straight to Stit Out. Point it at an image or audio file and it uses multimodal AI to describe the photo or transcribe the audio directly into the output.

sections.title: Codebase to Course
paragraphs: If you've been vibe coding your way through a project and have no real idea how it actually works, codebase to course fixes that. It's a clawed code skill that takes your entire codebase and generates a single page interactive HTML crash course from it. Plain English translations, metaphors, visualizations, and quizzes, all rendered directly in the browser using Claude's HTML artifacts.

sections.title: mac-code
paragraphs: Claude Code is powerful, but the API bill at the end of a heavy session is real. Mac code runs the same autonomous terminal agent workflow entirely on Apple silicon for free using flash streaming and KV cache compression. It fits 35 billion parameter mixture of experts models like Quen 3.5 into 16 GB of unified RAM and hits 30 tokens per second through llama.cp and MLX backends full web search file tools and shell access all local.

sections.title: fyn
paragraphs: Finn is a community fork of UV written in Rust that keeps everything that made UV worth using. Fast dependency resolution, virtual environment management, and PI project.l workflows guaranteed to stay independent and open source with active maintainers already shipping new features including fin shell, fin upgrade, and a native taskr runner built directly into PI project toml.

sections.title: lean-ctx
paragraphs: Watching an AI agent read 10,000 lines of npm build logs and knowing exactly what it's costing you per token is a specific kind of pain. Leanctx sits between your agent and everything it reads. A shell hook intercepts and compresses noisy CLI outputs before they hit the context window. An MCP server handles cached file reads and generates smart dependency maps.

sections.title: skills
paragraphs: Sahil of India open sourced the entire methodology from the minimalist entrepreneur as executable clawed code skills. Nine skills you install directly into your terminal. Validate idea scope MVP first customers pricing and more. Invoke one and your AI applies Sahil's exact framework to your specific situation interactively rather than you trying to extract advice from a book and apply it yourself.

sections.title: pgmicro
paragraphs: Seekite is convenient but you lose Postgress syntax and type system. PG micro closes that gap. It's an experimental fork of terso the from scratch rust rewrite of SQLite that gives you a fully inprocessed RESQL implementation. The clever part is how it handles parsing. Instead of translating SQL syntax or compiling Postgress to web assembly, it extracts the actual native parser directly from the Postgress SQL source code using lib pgor query.

sections.title: Advertising Skills for AI Agents
paragraphs: Most AI generated marketing copy sounds like AI generated marketing copy because it's pulling from generic patterns with no real advertising expertise behind it. Advertising skills packages, Kim Barrett's Facebook ads and lead generation frameworks directly into runnable agent skills. load them into your terminal and your AI can analyze ad copy, review campaign structures, calculate rows, and generate hooks based on frameworks that have actually converted in the real world.

sections.title: repo-task-proof-loop
paragraphs: Most autonomous coding sessions drift or stall on complex projects. Repo task proof loop keeps them on track. Give it a large task and it automatically generates strict acceptance criteria. It spawns sub agents to write the code, checks their work against the spec, resets the context window intelligently to avoid token burn, and loops until every bug is resolved. The creator ran codec sessions up to 12 hours straight on complex projects using this exact workflow.

sections.title: daVinci-MagiHuman
paragraphs: Synchronized AI video and audio usually means two separate models awkwardly stitched together and the seams show. Da Vinci Magic Human uses a single stream transformer that processes text, video, and audio tokens in one shared sequence. The result is performance-grade human avatars with synchronized speech, expressive facial movements, and realistic body motion generated as a unified output rather than separate pipelines merged in post.

sections.title: Awesome-PhD-CV
paragraphs: Awesome. PhD CV provides ATS optimized latex templates tested specifically against the parsers that eat multicolumn layouts, custom fonts, and special glyphs for breakfast. Alongside the industry ready templates, it includes full academic CV versions and guidelines on how to frame research experience and open-source GitHub projects for hiring managers who don't speak academic.

sections.title: ClawLink
paragraphs: Claw Link is an AI agent social network where your personal AI avatar connects directly with other people's agents. Instead of messaging a colleague to find a meeting time, you tell your agent to ask theirs. The two agents negotiate autonomously in seconds and hand you the result. When something gets ambiguous, a built-in escalation mechanism kicks it back to the human owner before anything goes sideways.

sections.title: Citadel
paragraphs: Citadel was built after running nearly 200 autonomous agents across a production codebase with 27 postmortems worth of hard lessons baked directly into the framework. An intent router classifies the task and routes it through one of four orchestration tiers, always picking the cheapest tool. Simple fixes go through a lightweight skill. Complex work escalates to fleet mode where multiple parallel agents spin up simultaneously in isolated git work trees.

sections.title: Ladder
paragraphs: Ladder gives AI agents a structured pipeline modeled on the scientific method rather than single turn prompts. Instead of just answering simple prompts, it runs an endless loop while you sleep, forming testable hypotheses, running structured experiments, and automatically feeding verified results right back into your project. Just point it at your code base and let your AI agents run wild.

sections.title: cc-skills-golang
paragraphs: General purpose AI coding assistants make predictable mistakes in Go. CC Skills Golang fixes that with 35 plus domain specific skills built for production. Golang language conventions, common errors, testing, benchmarks, security, and observability all covered. The creator distilled these from real world Go project commits and human reviewed every single one to keep AI slop out.

sections.title: design-dna
paragraphs: Design DNA takes a reference UI, whether a screenshot, image, or live URL, and reverse engineers it into a quantified design DNA JSON file. It goes deeper than grabbing hex codes. It extracts across three dimensions. Measurable design system tokens like typography and spacing, qualitative design style covering brand mood and interaction feel, and visual effects including canvas, WebGL, shaders, and animations.

sections.title: koe
paragraphs: CO is a voice input tool for Mac OS with no guey, no electron, and no subscription. Press a global hotkey, speak, and the transcript gets cleaned up by an AI model and pasted directly into whatever app you're using. The architecture is Rust Core with native Apple APIs for hotkeys and clipboard management. Under 15 megabytes on disk, under 20 megabytes of RAM.

sections.title: FlyAI Skill
paragraphs: Planning travel usually means a dozen open tabs comparing flights, hotels, and pricing across different platforms. Fly a skill is an MCP plugin that gives your AI agent real-time access to Fliggy's full inventory. Flights, luxury hotels, local attractions, and ground transport, all from the terminal. No API key registration, no developer account setup. It plugs directly into cloud code and open claw.

sections.title: MiroShark
paragraphs: Miroshark is a multi- aent swarm intelligence engine built on docker and neo forj. Spawn dozens of specialized AI workers with shared memories, sandboxes, and custom tools. Agents dynamically form teams and coordinate on tasks too complex or timeconuming for a single LLM to handle alone. deep PR analysis, complex code generation, all parallelized across a coordinated swarm from a few terminal commands.

sections.title: TRIBE v2
paragraphs: Meta's AI research team open-sourced Tribe V2. It's a multimodal foundation model trained on over a thousand hours of real fMRI recordings that predicts how the human brain responds to text, audio, and video across 70,000 neural voxels. Using Llama 3.2 2 and VJA 2. Under the hood, it can zero predict brain activity for a completely new subject reacting to a completely new video it has never seen.

sections.title: TurboQuant+
paragraphs: The KV cache memory wall is the hard limit that ends most long local AI sessions. Google research dropped a paper on Turbo Quant, a three-bit compression algorithm that shrinks the KV cache by up to 6x with no accuracy loss. Turboquant Plus is a fork that brings the algorithm to Apple silicon and llama.cpp. CPP using custom metal kernels achieving 4.6x memory compression with no speed penalty. [music]
